rationale: browser-use is a mature, production-grade browser automation framework (~167 Python files in source core, 46 directories, 89 tests, 113 examples) with deep architectural depth. It implements event-driven browser management via bubus event bus and CDP (via cdp-use). Key capabilities directly relevant to Veridian: (1) Structured JSON Schema extraction via dynamic Pydantic model generation (schema_utils.py); (2) Self-healing selectors via enhanced DOM snapshots with accessibility tree and paint-order filtering (dom/service.py, dom/serializer/); (3) Stealth/anti-bot via cloud browser integration, captcha watchdog, proxy rotation, and security watchdogs; (4) LLM-driven script generation via agent system prompts and beta Rust agent integration; (5) Queue/job scheduling via Agent step loop with planning, message compaction, and follow-up tasks. Tier A (not S) because while architecturally deep, it is a complete agent framework rather than a focused extraction/scraping engine — structured extraction is one capability among many, and JSON-LD/Schema.org microdata extraction is not natively implemented.
limitations: No native JSON-LD / Schema.org microdata extraction — only general JSON Schema extraction via LLM
No built-in fuzzy matching / dedupe pipeline — relies on LLM for duplicate detection
No full-text search index — only runtime page search via SearchPageAction
Queue / job scheduling is in-process Agent step loop, not a persistent/distributed queue
Stealth capabilities primarily via cloud service (browser-use-cloud), not fully local
Self-healing is DOM snapshot + accessibility tree based; no explicit selector mutation/fallback engine
Script generation is LLM-prompt driven, not a separate script synthesis / compilation pipeline
Beta Rust agent integration exists but is experimental/opt-in
